description: Stereo output stage for the C1 channel strip, with four saturation engines, pan, dim and mute, a level meter, a loudness reading and a goniometer

params.text: Sets how hard the chosen saturation engine is pushed, 0% to 100%; on the Standard engine it does nothing in Master Output mode and adds at most 0.8dB of level in Channel Output mode
Shifts the tone of the 2520, 8816 and DM2+ engines, 0% to 100%; the Standard engine never reads it
Pans between the two channels; in Master Output mode the centre position loses 3dB, and in Channel Output mode the centre is unity
Sets the output level, -60dB to 0dB in Master Output mode and -60dB to +6dB in Channel Output mode, slewed so a fast change does not click
Drops the output by the amount set on the menu, -12dB when the module is added, and lights while it is down
Silences the output over about 8ms, and lights while it is silent

inputs.text: The left input, and the source for the right channel as well while the right input is unpatched
The right input; with nothing patched here the left input feeds this channel too

outputs.text: The left channel after pan, level, the saturation engine, mute, dim and the menu’s trim; the engine clips at ±10V but the trim is applied after it
The right channel after pan, level, the saturation engine, mute, dim and the menu’s trim; the engine clips at ±10V but the trim is applied after it

notes: The four small squares above the display choose the saturation engine, in the same order as the menu's Character Engine list.
The small square at the top right of the display turns the goniometer drawing off.
A freshly added module is on the Standard engine in Master Output mode, and in that state neither DRIVE nor CHAR changes the sound at all.
Each jack carries one channel, so a polyphonic cable is reduced to its first channel.
CHO-X adds voltage control of the level, pan, drive and character, and has to be placed immediately to the right of this module.
menu: Trim — a slider setting a final gain after everything else, -12dB to +12dB
Dim gain — a slider setting how far the D button drops the output, -30dB to -1dB, rounded to whole dB
Character Engine: Standard, 2520, 8816, DM2+ — chooses the saturation model; each of the last three carries its own OFF, 2×, 4× and 8× oversampling choice
Operating Mode: Master Output, Channel Output — sets the VOLUME knob's top to 0dB or +6dB and changes the pan law and the Standard engine's drive
ON — under Peak Hold, keeps the meter's brightest segment showing the loudest recent peak; it is on when the module is added
Hold Time: 0.5s, 1.0s, 1.5s, 2.0s, 3.0s, 5.0s — under Peak Hold, sets how long that peak is held before it starts falling
Fall Rate: 12 dB/s (slow), 24 dB/s (medium), 48 dB/s (fast), 96 dB/s (instant) — under Peak Hold, sets how fast the held peak falls

inputs.1:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the left input.
